title: A tested resolution of the black-hole information paradox

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a precise, independently validated account of what happens to quantum information when a black hole evaporates. It would establish whether evaporation preserves information through unitary quantum evolution or instead produces a specific, demonstrable departure from unitarity. The paradox arises because semiclassical gravity predicts thermal radiation and mass loss, while extrapolating the usual information-loss account through complete evaporation appears to turn a pure quantum state into a mixed state.

A resolution must explain information behavior beyond reproducing an entropy curve. The Page curve describes how the radiation's entanglement entropy evolves: information-preserving evaporation requires the late radiation to carry correlations that change the entropy evolution expected from a straightforward thermal description. Holographic calculations have made substantial progress on this problem, including explanations of interior encoding and reconstruction. Reproducing the Page curve alone, however, does not establish full unitary evolution of the quantum state.

Proposed scope: the defining advance would combine an explicit evaporation mechanism, a derivation of its entropy evolution, and a discriminating check independent of the calculation producing that curve. Independent mathematical validation and empirical confirmation would establish different things. A consistency result could strengthen a conceptual resolution; a physical observation would be required to claim empirical confirmation of its account of black-hole evaporation.

significance.text: An independently validated resolution would establish how information behaves in black-hole evaporation and impose a major consistency requirement on theories describing that regime. If information is preserved, the theory must explain how the apparent information loss of the semiclassical description is avoided. If unitarity fails, the departure must be specified and demonstrated. Either outcome would address a central conflict at the intersection of quantum mechanics and gravity.

The holographic setting makes the consistency issue particularly sharp: the boundary conformal field theory evolves unitarily, requiring its gravitational description to preserve information. Understanding how the bulk description realizes that requirement could clarify the relationship between spacetime geometry, entanglement, and information recovery. Extending such an account to physically relevant evaporation would require establishing which conclusions survive beyond the assumptions and boundary conditions of the model.

Scope synthesis: settling this paradox would constrain the relationship between gravity and quantum mechanics in evaporation, without determining their entire relationship. It would not by itself provide a laboratory witness that gravity is non-classical, a complete ultraviolet theory, traversable wormholes, or practical energy extraction. Broader theoretical insights could follow, but each additional scientific or technological consequence would require its own argument and evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is an account of evaporation precise enough to distinguish information preservation from a specified failure of unitarity, explain the relevant quantum-state evolution, and face a check that can discriminate between competing accounts. An entropy curve is an important constraint, but it does not by itself establish the complete information mechanism or prove full unitary evolution. The supplied evidence supports substantial progress within holographic frameworks without establishing an independently tested account for real black holes.

A concrete theoretical barrier is understanding the assumptions and scope of reconstruction. Penington's calculation uses the Ryu–Takayanagi formula and entanglement wedge reconstruction, both holographic ingredients. Tiny, non-perturbative reconstruction errors play a crucial role. Immediately after the Page time, reconstructing interior operators from the radiation requires knowledge of the initial black-hole state; reconstruction over larger classes of states becomes possible later. This initial-state restriction applies to the specified reconstruction task and time, rather than to every aspect of the Page-curve derivation.

A separate observational barrier is the extremely weak Hawking radiation expected from astrophysical black holes. The supplied 2025 survey attributes the lack of experimental verification to this minuscule radiation. Demonstrating information behavior would require a discriminating physical consequence, beyond establishing thermal emission or reproducing a mode-mixing relation. The supplied sources identify no decisive observable for that purpose, so the feasibility of a direct test remains uncertain.

current_state.text: Geoffrey Penington's “Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction and the Information Paradox” was first submitted on 20 May 2019, revised on 29 August 2020, and published as JHEP 09 (2020) 002. It studies an evaporating black hole in AdS/CFT with absorbing boundary conditions. The calculation finds a transition in the quantum Ryu–Takayanagi surface at the Page time and derives a Page curve. These are theoretical results within the specified holographic setting, rather than measurements of astrophysical Hawking radiation.

The calculation also describes part of the interior as encoded in early radiation. Directly after the Page time, interior operators can be reconstructed from the radiation only when the initial black-hole state is known; later reconstructions can cover larger classes of states. Non-perturbative reconstruction errors are essential to the account. Penington presents a resolution of information-paradox and firewall questions within AdS/CFT, so the achievement should not be reduced to merely drawing an entropy curve. Its model-specific explanatory success and its applicability to real evaporating black holes remain distinct questions.

Ricardo Bulcão Valente Ferrari and Samuel Bueno Soltau's “Black Hole Thermodynamics: Established Results, Unresolved Paradoxes, and Speculative Resolutions” was submitted on 4 July 2025 and revised on 10 December 2025. The supplied record identifies it as an arXiv survey and contains no journal version. Its authors describe persistent information-paradox challenges, discuss islands and replica wormholes as proposals suggesting preservation of unitarity, and report a lack of experimental verification. They also distinguish reproducing the Page curve from proving full unitary evolution. These are the survey authors' assessments, rather than evidence of universal agreement across the field.

Evidence coverage limits the breadth of this account. The supplied review used Penington's abstract and a PDF extraction that ends during page 37; the retained primary-paper text is therefore partial. The survey extraction includes all 11 pages through its references. Although the source artifacts were retrieved on 1 November 2026, the supplied search record is empty. These materials establish the dated theoretical achievements and the survey's December 2025 assessment, but do not establish a comprehensive account of all relevant literature or measurements through 1 November 2026. That coverage gap does not invalidate the supported calculations or demonstrate that later results do not exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed theoretical demonstration: publish a framework that explicitly states whether evaporation preserves information, derives the late-time entropy from its own rules, and explains the associated quantum-state evolution or specific failure of unitarity. Its assumptions, boundary conditions, reconstruction requirements, and treatment of non-perturbative effects should be explicit enough for independent researchers to reproduce the argument and identify where it could fail. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed theoretical demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed independent validation: require a discriminating check beyond the calculation that generated the Page curve. An independently established consistency requirement that competing accounts fail could provide conceptual validation. Empirical validation would instead require a predicted physical consequence that is subsequently measured. Under this proposal, deriving a Page curve inside a model that assumes the relevant duality would be valuable evidence but would not alone complete the innovation.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed independent validation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed experimental boundary: an acoustic or optical analog reproducing a mode-mixing formula would qualify only if a justified theoretical connection showed that its result discriminates between accounts of gravitational evaporation. A framework's assertion that an analog is relevant would not suffice. The supplied evidence establishes neither such a decisive connection nor an existing feasible observable for an astrophysical test.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed experimental boundary

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements: independent analyses should reproduce the central derivation and assess its sensitivity to initial states, boundary conditions, and approximations. Any physical demonstration should state which systems, observables, and regimes it tests. A finite collection of successful calculations or observations would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, rather than literal universality across all black holes or a complete theory of quantum gravity.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements

related_concepts.text: Roster comparison: PHY-03, “A laboratory proof that gravity is non-classical,” addresses a different evidential target. PHY-11 asks how information behaves during black-hole evaporation; PHY-03 asks for a laboratory demonstration of non-classical gravity. Both concern the meeting of gravity and quantum physics, but completing either would not automatically complete the other. This distinction is based on the supplied roster title; a detailed PHY-03 record was not provided.

The strongest scientific overlaps are with quantum information and holography. Entanglement wedge reconstruction connects interior observables to information encoded in the radiation or boundary description, while the unitary boundary theory constrains the gravitational account. These tools and frameworks help formulate a resolution, but their use in a particular model does not itself supply independent empirical validation of evaporation.

Roster comparison: PHY-05, “A tested microphysical account of the dark-energy scale,” and PHY-12, “Experimental identification of the physics that sets the Higgs-mass scale,” likewise seek explanatory physics with discriminating evidence. Their targets are different: the dark-energy scale and Higgs-mass scale, respectively, rather than information evolution in black-hole evaporation. A resolution of PHY-11 would not, by itself, settle either scale problem. These are comparisons of the supplied concept titles, without an assertion that the entries share a mechanism.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish the full literature or measurement status through 1 November 2026; the freshness search record is empty.
No decisive observable or feasible direct experimental test of information behavior in astrophysical evaporation is established by the supplied sources.
The extent to which the specified AdS/CFT results extend to physically relevant black holes and different evaporation settings remains unestablished here.
The supplied record does not establish whether an existing independent consistency check would meet the proposed completion criteria; a blanket claim that no independent checks exist is unwarranted.
Penington's retained PDF extraction is partial, ending during page 37, which limits assessment of the paper's full arguments.
The completion criteria are proposals; agreement on what would constitute a sufficiently discriminating resolution is not established.
Detailed comparisons with PHY-03 and other roster entries remain limited by the absence of their full records.
